draft.title: Newton's first law
card: Newton's first law says an object keeps its velocity unless an unbalanced force acts on it. The unbalanced force is the net force, the sum of all the forces on the object.
If the forces are balanced, an object at rest stays at rest. A moving object keeps moving in a straight line at the same speed.
The tendency of an object to keep its state of motion is called inertia. In a car that stops suddenly, a passenger keeps moving forward until the seatbelt applies an unbalanced force to stop them.
An unbalanced force is needed to change the velocity, which means to speed up, slow down or turn. Motion alone does not need an unbalanced force.
draft.remember: Balanced forces mean no change in velocity. Inertia is the tendency to keep moving or stay at rest.

a.q: A skydiver falls at a steady 55 m/s straight down. Which statement about the forces on the skydiver is correct?
opts: They are balanced, so there is no unbalanced force
The unbalanced force points down, because of the motion
The unbalanced force points down, because of gravity
The unbalanced force points up, because of air resistance
a.why: Constant velocity means the velocity is not changing, so the forces are balanced. Gravity and air resistance both act, but they cancel. Motion downwards does not need an unbalanced force downwards.

b.q: In a level, straight hallway, a student pushes a trolley at a constant 1.5 m/s. What is true about the horizontal forces on the trolley?
opts: The push is balanced by the forces resisting the motion
The push is larger than the forces resisting the motion
The push is the only horizontal force acting on it
The push is balanced by the trolley's weight
b.why: The velocity is not changing, so the forces are balanced: the push equals friction and the other forces resisting the motion. A larger push would be an unbalanced force and the trolley would speed up. Weight acts downwards, not along the hallway, so it cannot balance a horizontal push.
b.clue: Is the trolley speeding up, slowing down or neither?

a.best: They are balanced, so there is no unbalanced force

b.best: The push is balanced by the forces resisting the motion
